biomes.note: sea floor below the datum: rocky bed; no face (sea cells take their naval group)
moisture splits grass (wet) from steppe (dry), rules.moisture
open and dry: Steppe keeps Pathfinder and WaterDiviner
lake bed; no face (lake cells take the Lake group)
Snow face and permanent snow only where permanentWhite holds (12 snow months)

layerSet.name: grass
layerSet.use: base, full weight everywhere; flora stripped

layerSet.name: mud
layerSet.use: marsh, rainforest wet ground, lake beds

layerSet.name: beach
layerSet.use: non-rocky coast band (ground_beach_a_s exists but is not flagged for_terrain)

layerSet.name: riverbed
layerSet.use: river and lake edges: the water-edge treatment for MMR-285

layerSet.name: mountain_rock
layerSet.use: exposed rock and the mountain landform

layerSet.name: permanent_snow
layerSet.use: permanent white only (permanentWhite); seasonal snow is the dynamic snow texture

notes: The shared biome table (MMR-248, docs/biome-presentation.md). One row per exported biome drives the navmesh face type (terrainType; playability.json cells.landFaceGroups must name the same type, which the travel compiler checks), the terrain layer mix (layers, fractions over layerSet names summing to 1), the battle class (battleClass; mission-scenes.json biomeClass must agree), the colour grade (colourGrade; colourGradeWet for grassland at or above rules.moisture.split; null for water, which takes the temperature band of climate-flow.json) and the snow treatment (seasonal: the dynamic snow texture follows the FWGC++ snow season; permanent: the permanent_snow layer and the Snow face all year). permanentWhite is the one mask for permanent white: its biomes (land_ice; snow is a tombstoned label) plus every land sample with snowMonths months of snow at or above snowThreshold; the same mask gives the Snow face. mutation is the live-mutation remap: a school retypes a mutated land face only within landValid (never Dune, Bridge, Fording, Beach, water or Mountain; passability never changes), coreOverrides refine a school per natural biome, hidden schools reuse a visible school's look and type (hiddenLooks), generated magic variants are visual only, and a mutated cell's battle class is mission-scenes.json faceClass[remapped type]; the thresholds are read per world from world.json. layerSet is the 15-slot template layer set (slot 15 free), composited from the highest slot down, with installed texture names verified against the installed packs (tools/check_layer_textures.py): full-colour textures only (MMR-249: the pale *_mainmap textures are not plain layers), scale the tile size in map units (15-20 suits biome layers; 5 reads as noise), tint the albedo factor (mode 1 adds, mode 2 only darkens). tools/scenebin/make_surface_template.py generates the template's material layers from it (no flora meshes, the same layer in every season, every layer flag off). rules are the target-fraction rules the layer compile applies (src/WorldBridge/src/terrain_layers.cpp, docs/terrain-compiler.md "Layers"): the biome row with the moisture split (the row's wet share at split, 1 at split + band, 0 at split - band), kernel smoothing within land or water, then cold, mountain, slope (slopeRock ramp; desertSlopeLayer on a Desert face), coast (rockyLayer by rocky_coast), water edge, ice cap and permanent white. alpha converts fractions to the stored bytes with the over-compositing inverse a_k = f_k / (f_0 + ... + f_k) (MMR-249: alpha-over, weight linear in the byte divided by smoothBlendAmount; slope transparency off). flora plants map trees (flora.bin) on the listed biomes: density per square unit at full flora-layer weight, scale range, clearances and a maxTrees cap that thins the density (MMR-247, acc4 V4: density 3.6 puts the planted trees per occupied 10-unit cell at the installed Main_map's quantiles, just under them; 0.45 left forests nearly bare after the flora-layer share, coast, pad and road clearances; maxTrees 88,000 is the count MMR-249 measured in game). slopeRock is scaled with projection.json verticalScale (0.01 -> 0.005 halves 0.6/1.2 to 0.3/0.6). Every exported biome id must appear here with the same core name, and every water_type, river and landform code must be listed; anything else fails. coastEpsilon (world units) keeps the compiled coastline coherent with the sea datum: ocean samples are lowered to at most -coastEpsilon and land samples raised to at least +coastEpsilon, which survives 16-bit quantization and the engine's 0.03 truncation toward zero. Lakes are left as compiled.
